_about: Tables for body/MUSCULAR.md. Rendered by build-body-data.py. Muscle groups are the functional model (anatomy real; the selection and the stats proposed). Activation profiles are illustrative percentages of maximal voluntary contraction (%MVC), read from EMG studies where one exists and the keeper's estimate where none does; every profile is a Composer-scale data task to refine (combat keeper's note, item 5). mark: rex | proposed | open. Tables moved whole to data/library/muscular.json (no game columns): values, fatigue_rates, endurance_time, training, adaptation, tendons.

groups.title: The muscle groups the sim tracks (left/right where the body has two)
groups.source: Anatomy is textbook (Gray's). The split by head (deltoid front/middle/rear; chest clavicular/sternocostal; and so on) is Rex's rule that groups split the way real muscles split (COMBAT.md 4b). Which groups count is proposed (ChatGPT's 25 to 40 functional model, extended). MUS-ANAT

activations.title: Action activation profiles (% of the group's maximum; illustrative)
activations.source: Shape from EMG literature where it exists (inverted row and suspension rows: lats, mid trapezius, biceps, rear deltoid at 50 to 60% MVIC; climbing postures: middle and lower trapezius 35 to 60%; MUS-EMG). Hauling rope is ChatGPT's illustrative profile (COMBAT.md 4b). Every other profile is the keeper's estimate and a data task to refine. The columns are the groups by id; a blank is 0.

patterns.title: Movement patterns (neural recruitment lives here, not per muscle and not in the skill)
patterns.source: ChatGPT's point (outside AI), kept: a man gets stronger at a movement by recruiting more of the muscle he has, without more muscle and without more skill; Swordplay is technique and timing, Reflexes is response speed, neither is maximal recruitment. The pattern set is the keeper's; each activation row names its patterns. Patterns that one arm performs are tracked per side (L/R), like the muscles, so handedness, a lost hand and one-sided training matter; the trunk and leg patterns are one.

injuries.title: Muscle and tendon injuries
injuries.source: Strain grading I to III is clinical standard; recovery times are typical ranges (textbook). Risk factors: fatigue, cold, no warm-up, a load far above the group's development, prior injury.

gym.title: The gym regimen (Rex's gym simulator): what a week looks like
gym.source: Rex: the character goes to the gym, designs a regimen and conducts it; pirates probably had no gyms, disbelief suspended (COMBAT.md 4b). The push/pull/legs/cardio/combat/rest week and the early equipment (stones, ropes, rowing, barrels, weapon drill) are ChatGPT's (proposed, outside AI). The minigame itself is Rex's to design (house rule).

limb_strength.title: How a limb's Strength is computed from its groups (proposed answer to the replace-or-compute question)
limb_strength.source: Rex left open whether muscle replaces per-limb Strength or Strength is computed from it (COMBAT.md 4b; ChatGPT: replaces). This table is the 'computed' reading, offered because it keeps STATS.md's Strength number alive for every system that already reads it while the muscles underneath make it per limb and trainable by what you do. Weights are the keeper's.
